newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: GROWING LABOR BLACK MARKET IN BUENOS AIRES-REPORT.
newsitem.headline: GROWING LABOR BLACK MARKET IN BUENOS AIRES-REPORT.

text.p: The number of black market workers in greater Buenos Aires grew in May to a record high of 1.2 million, according to official data published Wednesday by Clarin newspaper.

A previous half-yearly poll by state-run INDEC institute showed that last October the unregistered workers, who have no social security coverage and who do not pay taxes, totaled about 1.1 million in the area.

These represented 18.7 percent of all salaried employees in 1980 and rose steeply after a convertibility law which pegged the peso to the dollar was introduced in 1991, Clarin said. Now it stands at 38.1 percent of all salaried workers.
This ratio in the city of Buenos Aires stood at 31.8 percent in May.
Argentina has an official unemployment rate of 16.1 percent.
